messages:
nina_ops: heads up — multiple customers and our support queue reporting p99 spikes and timeouts since the driver/firmware rollout yesterday. tickets reference model inference tail latencies and occasional API timeouts. example customer: acme-bio; they sent request ids and traces. opening thread for triage.

oncall-bot: ALERT: p99 latency > 2s in region us-west-2 for model-route (since 2024-12-03T04:12Z). Incident created: INC-2024-214. Pager: maria_sre.

jun_support: link to ticket: https://support.redwood.example/t/ACME-1023 — attaching customer snippet and the request ids they provided. They see spikes at ~04:15-04:40 UTC.

alex_enginfra: quick q — are these nodes showing high I/O wait? can someone paste iostat -x or nvme stats from an affected host (gpu-uw2-07)? suspect host kernel / NVMe pathing change after driver update.

maria_sre: i'm on it, collecting metrics from the span. p95 is up ~200ms, p99 up ~1.6s in spike windows. correlating with host background jobs. grabbing top/iostat now.

sasha_infra: pulled iostat for gpu-uw2-07; here's the snapshot around the spike window:

```
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1          0.00  0.50 12.00 34.00 1024.0  2048.0  92.0     8.9     25.3  6.0     28.5  1.50  90.2
```

Also saw concurrent fio-like jobs from scheduled quantization/bench pipelines on that host.

eli_prod_support: that matches our deployment timeline — we ran a controlled GPU firmware + driver rollout yesterday in batches (batch=10). timeline lines up with first customer reports.

alex_enginfra: possible causes: new driver (525.17) changed NVMe write path or exposes a kernel IO scheduler interaction; could be write amplification or unexpected merging. quick repro we can run during load to capture stacks:

```
sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 60
perf script | c++filt | head -n 40
```

but for mitigation, we should stop the rollout and roll back affected hosts, and pin traffic away from those nodes/region.

maria_sre: immediate mitigation executed: paused the rollout and rolled back driver to 522.09 on 5 sample hosts in us-west-2. p99 returned to baseline after rollback. scheduling rollback for remaining affected hosts in region.

nina_ops: :thumbsup: coordinate with deploy team and support for customer comms. please prepare a short status blurb for affected customers.

jun_support: sent update to acme-bio & others: "we are investigating a platform-level storage performance regression related to a recent host update; temporary mitigations (rollback/pin) applied, working on full remediation."

sasha_infra: additional investigation notes: strace on the model server shows long epoll_wait delays tied to read syscalls that are blocked on NVMe completion. kernel dmesg from some hosts contains repeated `nvme: timeout` messages around the time of the rollout.

alex_enginfra: next technical steps: collect fio reproducer for sustained io, run kernel bisect to isolate if it's kernel+driver interaction, validate rollback plan across autoscaler groups. short-term config tweaks to try on a subset: switch NVMe scheduler from mq-deadline -> none, tune nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us, and disable background quantization/bench jobs during rollouts.

maria_sre: created incident board and linked runbook. will also patch the autoscaler to avoid placing heavy offline jobs on hosts during driver rollouts.

eli_prod_support: note for finance/product: impacted customers will be eligible for SLA credits per policy. Support owners notified to include credit steps in follow-ups.

nina_ops: interim loop closed — rollback completed for us-west-2, monitoring for 1h. if stable we'll resume a controlled rollout with IO limits + no-background-jobs gating.

oncall-bot: INC-2024-214 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned owner: alex_enginfra for root cause.

maria_sre: logs and artifacts uploaded to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incident/INC-2024-214/artifacts.tar.gz (includes iostat, dmesg, perf samples).

alex_enginfra: i'll open an RFC for kernel & rollout gating changes and assign action items: sasha_infra for collecting full kernel traces, jun_support for customer comms templates, nina_ops for rollout playbook updates.

nina_ops: thanks everyone. add any remaining action items here and we'll keep this thread as the single source for the incident until the postmortem is published.
